solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Since very cold, I swallowed last of food mixed (10)

indicators.note: the last of anything is its final part, so only the closing letter of 'food' is taken

blocks.note: C = cold, as on a tap

annotation.surface: Someone, feeling very cold, gulped down the last of a food mixture.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Very cold' reads as one idea but splits in two, and 'mixed' looks like an anagram signal when it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the social sense: people who mixed together, keeping company, associated with one another.

clue.text: Endlessly false and at heart wrong too (4)

indicators.note: without ends, so 'false' loses both its first and last letters
a thing's heart is its centre, so only the middle letter of 'wrong' is used

blocks.note: fALSe without its first and last letters

annotation.surface: A complaint that something is false and wrong as well.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Too' sits at the end looking like an intensifier for 'wrong', but it is the definition, and 'and' is only a joining word.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: 'me too' and 'me also' both add one more to a list.

clue.text: Singular poll choice (9)

annotation.surface: An odd or unusual choice made at a vote.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Singular' reads as strange, describing the choice, but it is only the grammar abbreviation used in dictionaries.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a shop's range of goods to choose from is its choice or its selection.

clue.text: Compass that goes around? (13)

blocks.note: read as the drawing instrument with a point and a pencil, and meant in its older sense of an extent or boundary
read as the compass swinging round to draw a circle, and meant as the boundary line itself, which runs all the way round

annotation.surface: A drawing compass, the tool that swings round to draw a circle.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the instrument is a red herring; the compass that goes around is the line a compass draws.
annotation.definitionFit: Compass also means bounds or extent, and the bounding line that encircles a figure is its circumference.

clue.text: Given poster to cover hospital room no. 5? (7)

indicators.note: a poster covers a wall; here the poster's letters cover, or go around, what follows

blocks.note: an ad is a poster, split A…D
a ward is a room in a hospital
E is letter number five of the alphabet

annotation.surface: A patient is handed a poster to hang in hospital room number five.
annotation.walkthrough: The room's number reads as a label on the door, but it stands for the fifth letter of the alphabet.
annotation.definitionFit: A synonym by example: a prize awarded to someone has been given to them.

clue.text: Go off northwards, following mostly uniform notional line (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue north is upward, so ROT is written bottom to top
to follow is to come after, so the reversed word is placed after the shortened one
most but not all, so 'equal' loses its last letter

blocks.note: EQUAL, uniform, minus its last letter
to rot is to go off, as food does; turned up to TOR

annotation.surface: Food going off somewhere north of a vaguely even imaginary line.
annotation.walkthrough: The geography of 'northwards' and 'line' looks like part of the definition, but northwards is only the instruction to turn a word upside down.
annotation.definitionFit: The equator is imaginary: a line drawn on maps and globes that exists nowhere on the ground, hence notional.

clue.text: Couch found in contents of attic (4)

indicators.note: the contents of something are what it holds, so the answer is held inside the letters of the phrase

annotation.surface: An old couch turned up when clearing out the loft.
annotation.walkthrough: The indicator itself holds the answer, spanning three words including 'contents'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: couch and sofa are both the upholstered seat for two or more people in a living room.

clue.text: Theatre work by English artist (5)

blocks.note: RA = Royal Academician, a recognised artist

annotation.surface: A play credited to an English painter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Theatre work' reads as a single phrase, but 'work' belongs to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by genre: opera is a branch of theatre, drama set to music.

clue.text: Amazed, for instance, by massive weight I cast off (10)

blocks.note: a ton is a massive weight
to shed is to cast off

annotation.surface: Someone amazed at how much weight they have lost.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a dieter's delight; 'cast off' reads as losing the weight, and it does its job at the end of the word.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe the jaw-dropping reaction to something unexpected.

clue.text: Take flight circling left of the sun (5)

indicators.note: a bird circling a spot flies round it, so the word for flying goes round the letter

blocks.note: to soar is to take flight, split SO…AR

annotation.surface: An instruction to fly off and circle leftward around the sun.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Take flight' can mean flee, but here it means rise into the air.
annotation.definitionFit: Solar is the adjective for the sun, as in solar panel or solar eclipse.

clue.text: Tampered with mate’s menu for fun (9)

indicators.note: something tampered with has been interfered with, so the letters no longer stand in their original order

annotation.surface: A prankster altered a friend's menu as a joke.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'mate’s' is ignored; only the letters count.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something done for fun is done for amusement.

clue.text: Decline a copy, a flawed compendium of knowledge (13)

indicators.note: a flawed thing is faulty or out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Refusing a copy of a reference book because it is faulty.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Decline' looks like the start of the definition, but the whole phrase up to 'flawed' is fodder. Note the British spelling with AE.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: an encyclopaedia gathers knowledge on every subject into one work, which is what a compendium is.

clue.text: Wasn’t able to consider boxing essentially wildly (7)

indicators.note: to box something is to put it in a box, so one word encloses the other
the essence of a thing is its core, so only the central letters of 'wildly' are taken

blocks.note: to count someone lucky is to consider them so; split COU…NT
the middle two letters of wiLDly

annotation.surface: Someone could not bring themselves to think about boxing wildly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boxing' reads as the sport, and 'wildly' as an anagram signal, but neither is.
annotation.definitionFit: The contraction couldn't, could not, is the past of can't: exactly wasn't able to.

clue.text: Drink belonging to businesses under one ownership (5)

blocks.note: in = belonging to, as in 'in the club'

annotation.surface: A drink sold by all the outlets of one company.
annotation.walkthrough: CHA is British slang for tea, a word crosswords lean on often.
annotation.definitionFit: A business sense: a chain of shops or hotels is a set of outlets owned by one company, linked like chain links.

clue.text: Helps a small son, one pursued by extremes of slyest scavengers (10)

indicators.note: to be pursued is to have something coming after you, so the later pieces follow the earlier
the extremes of a thing are its two ends, so the first and last letters of 'slyest' are taken

blocks.note: S = small, as in clothing sizes

annotation.surface: A little boy being chased by sly scavengers, and someone helping him.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Helps' reads as a verb but is a plural noun: helps are helpers, a usage found in phrases like home helps.
annotation.definitionFit: A noun sense: a help, like a home help, is a person who assists, so helps are assistants.

clue.text: Heartless son, even though nourished, showed contempt (7)

indicators.note: without a heart means without a centre, so 'son' loses its middle letter

blocks.note: if = even though, as in 'pleasant, if dull'

annotation.surface: An ungrateful son sneered even after being fed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' reads as cruel, describing the son, but it removes his centre.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to sniff at something is to dismiss it with contempt, often with an audible sniff.

clue.text: Dodges ball game (7)

blocks.note: a dodge is a scam or fiddle, and so is a racket
a fast indoor game for two, an ancestor of squash, played against walls with a hard ball

annotation.surface: Someone ducks out of playing a ball game.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dodges' reads as a verb, avoiding the game, but it is a plural noun. Rackets, the game, is the forerunner of squash.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: rackets are dishonest schemes, or dodges, and rackets is also the name of a court game with a hard ball.

clue.text: Being distraught, exit scene (9)

indicators.note: someone distraught is upset and in disorder, so the letters are thrown out of order

annotation.surface: Someone upset leaving the scene, as an actor might.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Being' reads as a participle opening a phrase, 'being distraught', but it is the noun definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A noun sense: being, as in 'come into being', is the state of existing.

clue.text: Disregarded problematic region by delta (7)

indicators.note: a problematic region is in trouble, so its letters are disordered
one thing by another sits beside it, so D is placed next to the rearranged letters

blocks.note: Delta is D in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A troubled river delta region neglected by the authorities.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Delta' reads as a river mouth, fitting the region, but it is only a radio-alphabet letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: advice ignored has been disregarded, paid no attention.

clue.text: Not affected by rain in river (7)

indicators.note: one thing in another is inside it, so the word for rain goes within the river

blocks.note: the Dee is a river in Britain; split DE…E
to spit is to rain lightly

annotation.surface: Something unharmed by the rain falling into a river.
annotation.walkthrough: The Dee flows through Wales and England, and another runs through Aberdeen; crosswords use it constantly.
annotation.definitionFit: A preposition sense: 'we went despite the rain' means we went, not affected by the rain.

clue.text: Group of lions devouring first bits of our vegetable supply (7)

indicators.note: what is devoured ends up inside, so the lions' word swallows the letters
the first bit of each word is its opening letter

blocks.note: a pride is a group of lions; split PR…IDE

annotation.surface: Lions gobbling up the vegetables meant for us.
annotation.walkthrough: Lions do not eat vegetables, which is the joke; 'supply' reads as a noun, a store of food, but is the verb definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to supply food is to provide it.

clue.text: Expressions of stages in growth involving resistance (7)

indicators.note: to involve something is to include it, so the stages take the letter within them

blocks.note: phases are stages of development; split PH…ASES

annotation.surface: Faces or expressions changing through stages of growing up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Expressions' suggests faces, but it is meant in the verbal sense, as in a turn of phrase.
annotation.definitionFit: A verbal sense: a set expression such as 'over the moon' is a phrase.

clue.text: Whale oil process (5)

blocks.note: an archaic name for oil rendered from whale blubber, also called by the same word plus 'oil'
a series of connected steps, the word used for a sequence of thought or of events

annotation.surface: How oil is extracted from whales.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface asks how whale oil is made, but 'process' is a separate definition, not a description of the first. Train oil is the old whalers' term.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: train is an archaic word for whale oil, and a train of events is a process running in sequence.

clue.text: Concur in mature years about religious education (5)

indicators.note: about means around, so the years go around the school subject

blocks.note: RE = religious education, a school subject

annotation.surface: Coming to agree about religious teaching later in life.
annotation.walkthrough: RE is religious education, a subject taught in British schools.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: two people who concur share the same opinion, and so agree.

clue.text: Told to go round originally really very annoying attendant (7)

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the word for 'told to go' goes round the letters
at the origin of each word, so its opening letter is taken

blocks.note: someone told to go has been sent; split SE…NT

annotation.surface: An irritating attendant being ordered to leave.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Told to go round' reads as one command, but 'round' is the container signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a servant attends on a household, and an attendant is one who serves.

clue.text: Without the French ship propelled by steam (4)

annotation.surface: A French steamship lacking something.
annotation.walkthrough: The long phrase about steam is just a roundabout way of naming the two-letter ship prefix.
annotation.definitionFit: A preposition sense: 'a year less a day' means a year without a day.

clue.text: Dubiously reinsures races for two-year-old horses (9)

indicators.note: done dubiously means done in a doubtful, irregular way, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A shady insurer covering racing for young horses.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is specialist horse-racing language, so the anagram is the easier route in.
annotation.definitionFit: A racing term: a nursery is a handicap race confined to two-year-olds, the youngest horses racing.

clue.text: Frolic of little fish around noon (5)

indicators.note: the fish swims around, surrounding the letter

blocks.note: a dace is a small freshwater fish; split DA…CE

annotation.surface: Small fish playing about in the midday sun.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Frolic' reads as the fish's playing, a verb, but the definition is the noun.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: a frolic is a lively caper, and a dance is the same sort of joyful movement.

clue.text: Walk dogs, say, in retirement (4)

indicators.note: to retire is to withdraw or go back, so the word is written backwards

blocks.note: dogs are an example of pets

annotation.surface: A pensioner walking the dogs.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is someone's retired life, but 'in retirement' is the signal to go backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb sense: to step somewhere, as in 'step outside', is to walk there.

clue.text: Rags sewn perhaps clumsily with hem initially overlooked (10)

indicators.note: done clumsily means done in a muddle, so the letters are jumbled
at the start, so only the first letter of 'hem' counts
something overlooked is left out, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: the first letter of Hem, the letter removed

annotation.surface: Rags that have been sewn clumsily, the hem left unfinished.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rags' looks like part of the needlework, but it is the definition; and 'perhaps' is fodder, not a hint.
annotation.definitionFit: A slang sense: a rag is a disparaging word for a low-grade newspaper, as in 'the local rag'.
